column3: The written Hebrew reads “Jehoaddan,” the reading tradition “Jehoaddin”; NASB has “Jehoaddin.”
“Secure” is rendered “firmly,” and “struck down” as “killed … slain.”
“Let us look one another in the face” is rendered “let us face each other.”
“Animal of the field” is rendered “wild beast,” and “to a wife” as “in marriage.”
“Your heart has lifted you” is rendered “your heart has become proud,” and “be honored” as “Enjoy your glory.”
“Looked one another in the face” is rendered “faced each other.”
“Articles” is rendered “utensils,” and “sons of the pledges” as “hostages.”
“Rebellious” (Hebrew מֹרֶה) is rendered “bitter,” and “shut up and freed” as “bond nor free.”
The Hebrew “to Judah in Israel” is difficult; NASB renders “recovered for Israel, Damascus and Hamath, which had belonged to Judah.” The meaning is uncertain.
“Lay down” is rendered “slept,” and NASB adds “even.”
